regular.note:
N: the diagonal runs one cell per row, centred on the bar row
the old 2-cell steps made a knot at the stem.
a: the mark's square bowl plus a spur at the foot. The old cut-corner a read as o in words.

e: the bar stops short, so the aperture is 2 cells and the foot is no longer a 3x2 block.
The bar still meets the foot in one 2x2 corner (allow=block): four rows leave no other way.

s: corners cut like S
12 cells instead of 14, so it stops reading bold in running words.
t: starts one row below the cap line, so t and l no longer share a height (little, tools).
x: four wide, so the two strokes cross on a 2x2 centre (allow=block).

zero: cut corners and a centre dot on the bar row. The slash read as a heavy Ø at 120 px
0 and O now differ by 5 cells.
two: a hooked top (left terminal on row 2), right stem, then one diagonal step per row to the foot. The square 2 was a mirrored S and the plain diagonal 2 rhymed with Z (lead review, SEED 4127).
six: the top turns in on a diagonal, so 6 never reads as G (they differed by 2 cells).

seven: one even diagonal step per row into a straight stem
the old 2-1-3 staircase looked broken.

nine: six turned 180 degrees
the diagonal tail also separates 9 from g and q.
comma: head on the baseline, tail down-left. The same drawing as the apostrophe.
question: the hooked top of the 2, so the two shapes rhyme.
hyphen, dashes, operators and arrows all centre on row 4 (the mark's bar row).
slash: a cell of air on the left and two on the right, so 12/12 has a 2-cell gap on both sides at the tightest row.
backslash: spaced like slash.

asterisk: six arms from one centre cell
the old 17-cell star was the darkest glyph in the font.
percent: its two dots are 2x2 squares, not strokes (allow=block).
less: 3 wide, set in a 6-cell box (lsb 1, rsb 2) so < and > sit on the figure pitch.
greater: 3 wide in a 6-cell box, like less.
asciitilde: a 3-row wave so it centres on the bar row like the other operators.
periodcentered: on row 4, the mark's bar row, the centre of caps and figures.
multiply: 5x5 on the bar row, so 64x64 no longer reads as a lowercase x.
bullet: a 3x3 square dot centred on the bar row (allow=block).

arrow NE: head arms 2 cells past the tip, like the arrows' heads. The shaft lands in the corner
of the head, which makes one 2x2 (allow=block).
quoteright: the comma, raised to the cap line (head 2 cells, tail down-left).
quoteleft: quoteright turned 180 degrees.

bold.note: space: 4 cells in Bold, one more than Regular, to match the wider letters.
K: arm and leg step two cells per row, meeting the stem on the bar row.
N: widened to 8 so the diagonal can step two cells wide without filling the counter.
Q: the tail cuts the bottom-right corner, two cells wide, as in Regular.
R: the leg steps out two cells wide from the bar row.
V: straight for four rows, then two-cell steps to a three-cell point.
Y: six wide, like T, so the two-cell stem sits dead centre.
f: the hook overlaps the stem by one cell so the top stays joined.
i: a two-cell dot over a two-cell stem.
k: arm reaches the right edge, leg steps back from the bar-row junction.

s: five wide
the spine overlaps by one cell. The six-wide s was the darkest letter in a word.
t: one row below the cap line, as in Regular.
zero: cut corners and a one-cell centre dot (allow=thin): no slash blob.
one: stem centred in the 7-cell tabular box, flag and foot one cell either side.
two: hooked top, right stem, two-cell diagonal steps, as in Regular.
six: diagonal top terminal, two cells per step.
seven: even two-cell diagonal steps into the stem.
dots are 2x2 in Bold. A 2x1 dot read as a dash (2.1 - TILE).
comma: the 2x2 dot with a tail, the same drawing as quoteright.
question: the hooked top of the bold 2 over a 2x2 dot.
slash: spaced like Regular.
backslash: spaced like slash.
percent: 2x2 dots and a two-cell slash.

at: the inner a keeps one-cell details
at two cells it would fill solid.
less: 5 wide in an 8-cell box, the bold figure pitch.
greater: 5 wide in an 8-cell box, like less.

periodcentered: a 2x2 dot cannot centre on one row
it sits on rows 4-5, where the x-height and caps share most.

degree: a small ring
its one-cell sides keep the hole open.
arrows: two-cell head steps on a one-cell shaft, like a bold horizontal.

arrowup: two-cell stem
the head flares one step per row.

arrow NE: a solid right-angled head on a two-cell shaft
open arms clogged at two cells.
